about: Pose prompts for Edric, the player's knight: a rider and his horse, posing together. {pose} in the base is replaced by a pose's text. Every pose takes his standing image (art/source/edric-stand.jpg) as its one reference. 4:3, because horse and rider are wide. The lance attacks with a charge: ready, wind-up (couching the lance), thrust, follow-through, recover; the gallop is four poses.
base: The exact same knight and horse as the reference: the same young knight with a calm face and short light brown hair, white and gold heavy plate armour, a helm with the visor up and a tall blue plume, a blue cape, a kite shield on his left arm and a long white lance; the same white warhorse wearing white and gold barding with blue trim and blue tassels; same colours, same art style, same size in frame. Strict side view facing right. Pose: {pose}. He holds exactly one lance: no second lance, no afterimage, no ghost or blurred copies. The horse has exactly four legs and one tail. A single sharp still frame: no motion blur, no speed lines, no smear, no dust, no sparks or effects. Horse, rider and lance entirely in frame with margin around them, all four hooves included, even studio lighting, no cast shadow. Plain flat pure green background (#00FF00), no green on the knight or the horse, no text, no ground.

ready.pose: gathering for the charge: the horse crouched back on its haunches with its head lowered and neck arched; the knight leaning forward in the saddle, the lance lowered toward level and pointing forward

wind-up.pose: couching the lance as the charge begins: the horse rising slightly with its front hooves lifting off the ground; the knight braced forward, the lance level and tucked under his right arm pointing straight ahead, shield raised

thrust.pose: the charge's impact: the horse lunging forward in full stride with its front legs stretched far forward; the knight standing in the stirrups and driving the lance straight forward at full reach

follow-through.pose: just after the impact: the horse's front hooves landing heavily; the knight leaning far forward over its neck, the lance still extended forward and tipped slightly down, cape swinging forward

recover.pose: reining back after the strike: the horse stepping back with its head raised and its weight on its hind legs; the knight sitting back upright, the lance swinging back up toward upright

gallop-1.pose: galloping to the right, the stretched phase: the horse's front legs reaching far forward and its hind legs pushing far back, its body long and low; the knight leaning forward with the lance level, pointing ahead, plume and cape streaming behind

gallop-2.pose: galloping to the right, the gathered phase: all four of the horse's hooves off the ground and tucked under its body, its back rounded; the knight leaning forward with the lance level, pointing ahead, plume and cape streaming behind

gallop-3.pose: galloping to the right, the landing phase: one hind hoof striking the ground, the other hind leg and both front legs folded forward in the air; the knight leaning forward with the lance level, pointing ahead, plume and cape streaming behind

gallop-4.pose: galloping to the right, the leading phase: one front hoof planted on the ground under the horse's chest, both hind legs swinging forward under its belly; the knight leaning forward with the lance level, pointing ahead, plume and cape streaming behind

hurt.pose: struck: the horse rearing up in alarm on its hind legs with its front hooves high in the air; the knight recoiling backward in the saddle, shield raised, the lance tilting back

fallen.pose: defeated: the horse down on its folded front knees with its head low; the knight slumped forward over its neck, head bowed, the lance lying on the ground beside them

victory.pose: triumph: the horse rearing proudly on its hind legs; the knight holding the lance high above his head in his right hand, shield arm raised, cape flowing
